# PR #297: PASS WITH NOTES, final round under C34

## Fix verification

The same real-cargo A -> B(build, then failed check) -> A reproduction that
returned B in round 1 now recompiles A and returns **A**, with
`--target aarch64-apple-darwin`. B's failed batch leaves `running B`;
returning A leaves `finished A`. A subsequent build reports 0.00 s, compiles
nothing, leaves source mtimes unchanged and still returns A.

The same runner verifies adoption: after B builds, a future-dated bare A stamp
is planted to reproduce the trusted legacy state. Corrected A touches,
recompiles and returns A; its next run is fresh. Thus the repair does not
silently retain a poisoned round-1 stamp.

An independent fake-cargo state oracle verifies that:

- Cargo observes `running <its tree>` before it executes.
- A waiting B cannot enter or replace A's running stamp while A holds the lock.
  SIGTERM drains A before B enters, and successful B publishes `finished B`.
- A batch failing after its first successful command leaves `running B` even
  when it wrote no deps artifact; returning A touches and publishes `finished A`.

The lock still encloses invalidation, running publication, every cargo command,
finished publication and copy-out. Cargo failure exits before `finished`;
copy-out failure may retain `finished` because the cargo artifacts are complete.
A target absent before the first cargo command has no trusted stamp to preserve.
The all-depth find detects explicit-target deps; its bookkeeping pruning does
not exclude the reproduced target-triple layout.

The committed 26-case suite now covers the missing layout, failed batches,
legacy adoption and newer bare-cargo triple/release artifacts. Its stamp-path
test also covers the reported symlink-to-directory behavior. Security owns the
separate C33 check/rename residual.
